text:
The Boring Company is building something far bigger than most people even realize

While everyone is focused on Tesla and SpaceX, Elon Musk is also transforming underground transportation and industrial infrastructure, and the scale of what’s now happening is incredible

The Boring Company is now valued at $23 billion after recently raising another $3 billion in funding

And that funding is helping accelerate something even massive: a new partnership to develop over 150 kilometers of underground infrastructure across the UAE, on top of the existing Dubai Loop project

Just look at what the company has already accomplished in Las Vegas:

• Over 4 MILLION passengers transported
• 14 operational stations
• 68 MILES of tunnels approved for expansion
• 123 stations approved across the planned network
• Targeting 28 operational stations by the end of 2026

And the expansion is already moving beyond Las Vegas

In Nashville, two Prufrock tunnel-boring machines are operating simultaneously, a third is scheduled to begin tunneling later this month, and a fourth is already being built

More than 40 stations are in various stages of planning and design

The company has also signed a new agreement to explore transportation and utility tunnels in Abu Dhabi

And just days ago, its massive 900,000-pound Prufrock-5 machine arrived in San Antonio to prepare for a new underground transportation project designed to improve accessibility

But here's another incredible example of how this technology is already being used inside Tesla's Gigafactory Texas

The Boring Company built an underground tunnel beneath an eight-lane highway to transport finished Cybertrucks directly from the production line to their staging area

Previously, that journey required around 12 minutes using surface roads

Now it takes just 60 SECONDS

That's a 12× improvement in transportation time

And the engineering behind the tunnels is even more impressive

The company has already demonstrated autonomous installation of massive concrete tunnel segments with millimeter precision, while its machines are designed to mine and install tunnel lining continuously

Think about what happens when this technology scales across factories, airports, cities and industrial infrastructure

And this is where the vision gets much bigger

The Boring Company is literally laying the foundation for 3D infrastructure for entire cities, where transportation networks expand across multiple underground levels instead of being limited to surface roads

Las Vegas, Nashville and Dubai are just the beginning

Elon Musk is fundamentally rethinking how cities will be built and how transportation will work at massive scale

And what he's building underground is going to be something far bigger than most people have ever imagined
